question: What is the primary definition of venepuncture in clinical practice?

options.A: The puncture of an artery to measure blood gases
options.B: The puncture of a vein with a hollow-bore needle to withdraw blood or administer fluids
options.C: The surgical incision of a vein to repair a vascular defect
options.D: The introduction of a catheter into the urinary bladder

explanation: Venepuncture specifically involves puncturing a vein using a hollow-bore needle to obtain blood samples, give IV fluids, or administer medications. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h1)

question: Before initiating a venepuncture procedure, what must the nurse verify?

options.B: The patient's identity using at least two unique identifiers
options.C: The expiration date of the hospital building
options.D: The exact cost of the laboratory reagents

explanation: Patient safety protocols dictate that nurses must always verify patient identity using at least two unique identifiers before starting any invasive procedure. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h1)

question: Which vein located in the antecubital fossa is generally considered the safest and most stable choice for routine venepuncture?
explanation: The median cubital vein is preferred for routine venepuncture because it is typically large, well-anchored, and less prone to movement. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h2)

question: How should a healthy, suitable vein feel upon physical palpation by the nurse?

options.D: Completely immobile and fixed to the bone

explanation: A healthy vein suitable for venepuncture feels bouncy, resilient, and refills promptly, whereas hard or pulsating vessels should be avoided. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h2)

question: Why is performing venepuncture on an arm with an active arteriovenous (AV) fistula strictly contraindicated?

options.A: It will cause severe pain but no permanent damage
options.B: It can permanently damage the dialysis access site and lead to severe complications
options.C: It causes immediate high blood pressure in the legs
options.D: It prevents the laboratory from running electrolyte tests

explanation: An AV fistula is a lifesaving access for hemodialysis; puncturing it can ruin the vascular access and cause critical complications, making it an absolute contraindication. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h3)

question: If a patient has had a radical mastectomy with lymph node dissection on their right arm, where should the nurse ideally perform venepuncture?

options.A: On the right arm to check lymphedema
options.B: On the left arm to prevent lymphedema and impaired healing
options.C: Directly over the surgical scar on the right arm
options.D: Venepuncture is completely banned for this patient anywhere on the body

explanation: An arm on the same side as a mastectomy with lymph node dissection is avoided to prevent lymphedema, making the opposite arm the correct choice. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h3)

question: Which of the following describes the relationship between needle gauge numbers and needle bore size?

options.A: A higher gauge number indicates a larger needle bore size
options.B: A lower gauge number indicates a larger needle bore size
options.C: Gauge numbers and needle bore sizes are unrelated
options.D: All gauges have the exact same bore size

explanation: In needle sizing, the gauge number is inversely related to the bore size; a lower gauge number means a larger needle diameter. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of a rigid, puncture-resistant sharps container at the bedside during venepuncture?

options.A: To store extra cotton swabs and alcohol wipes
options.B: To safely dispose of used needles immediately without recapping to prevent needle-stick injuries
options.C: To hold expired vacutainer tubes before discarding them
options.D: To collect blood samples for transport to the lab

explanation: Puncture-resistant sharps containers are specifically designed for the immediate, safe disposal of used needles without recapping to eliminate needle-stick injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h4)

question: Why must the antiseptic skin preparation be allowed to air dry completely before inserting the venepuncture needle?

options.A: To cool down the skin temperature
options.B: To allow time for antimicrobial action and prevent sample hemolysis and patient stinging
options.C: To make the skin easier to puncture with a blunt needle
options.D: To prevent the tourniquet from slipping off

explanation: Allowing the antiseptic to dry ensures it achieves maximum microbial kill and prevents both stinging for the patient and hemolysis of the blood sample. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h5)

question: What is the correct safety practice regarding used venepuncture needles?

options.A: Always recap the needle using both hands before disposal
options.B: Leave the needle on the bedside tray for housekeeping to clear
options.C: Never recap needles; activate safety devices and dispose of them immediately in a sharps container
options.D: Break the needle off the syringe before throwing it in the regular trash

explanation: To prevent accidental needle-stick injuries, nurses must never recap needles using two hands, but rather dispose of them immediately into a sharps container. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h5)

question: At what angle should the venepuncture needle be inserted into the skin and vein during the procedure?

options.D: 5 to 10 degrees parallel to the skin

explanation: Inserting the needle at a 15 to 30-degree angle ensures successful entry into the lumen of a superficial peripheral vein without puncturing through the back wall. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h6)

question: What is the primary reason for anchoring the vein by pulling the skin taut just before needle insertion?

options.B: To prevent the vein from rolling away from the needle
options.C: To increase the patient's blood pressure
options.D: To speed up the clotting process

explanation: Anchoring the skin stabilizes the vein and prevents it from rolling or shifting when the needle makes contact. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h6)

question: What immediate action should a nurse take if a hematoma begins to form during venepuncture?

options.A: Push the needle deeper into the tissue
options.B: Release the tourniquet, withdraw the needle, and apply firm pressure to the site
options.C: Inflate the blood pressure cuff above the site
options.D: Ignore it until the entire blood draw is completed

explanation: When a hematoma forms, the procedure must be stopped immediately by removing the tourniquet and needle, followed by firm pressure to stop internal bleeding. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h7)

question: Which of the following troubleshooting actions is strictly forbidden when blood fails to flow into the collection tube?

options.A: Gently adjusting the needle position slightly
options.B: Checking if the collection tube is fully pushed onto the holder
options.C: Aggressively probing and digging around with the needle in the tissue
options.D: Releasing the tourniquet and trying a new site

explanation: Aggressive probing causes immense patient discomfort, tissue trauma, and increases the risk of nerve damage, and must never be done. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h7)

question: Why should a nurse instruct a patient not to bend their elbow after venepuncture?

options.A: Bending the elbow stops blood flow to the fingers
options.B: Bending the elbow increases the risk of bruising and hematoma formation at the puncture site
options.C: It interferes with the laboratory machine reading
options.D: It causes the adhesive bandage to fall off immediately

explanation: Bending the arm increases pressure on the puncture site and tears the delicate vein wall, leading to bruising and hematomas. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h8)

question: When is the optimal time to label blood specimen collection tubes?

options.A: At the nursing station before entering the patient's room
options.B: At the patient's bedside immediately after blood collection
options.C: After returning from the laboratory at the end of the shift
options.D: Only after the laboratory results have been printed

explanation: To prevent misidentification errors, tubes must always be labeled at the patient's bedside immediately after the blood has been drawn. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h8)
